project.name: Online Examination Platform
project.summary: Web system for creating exams, delivering timed tests to students, and providing auto‑graded results.

functional_requirements: Teachers can create, edit, and delete question banks.
Teachers can schedule exams with start/end times and assign them to classes.
Students can take timed exams with automatic submission on timeout.
The system automatically grades objective questions and stores results.
Teachers and administrators can view exam results and analytics on a dashboard.
non_functional_requirements: The platform must prevent cheating through browser lockdown and monitoring.
The system must remain available and reliable throughout exam windows.
User interfaces must respond within 2 seconds for typical actions.
The architecture must scale to support concurrent exams for up to 5,000 students.

actors.name: Teacher
actors.description: Creates question banks, schedules exams, and reviews results.

actors.name: Student
actors.description: Logs in, takes assigned timed exams, and views personal results.

actors.name: Administrator
actors.description: Manages user accounts, system settings, and overall platform configuration.

use_cases.name: Create Question Bank
use_cases.description: Teacher adds, edits, or deletes questions and organizes them into banks.

use_cases.name: Schedule Exam
use_cases.description: Teacher defines exam parameters, selects a question bank, sets timing, and assigns to students.

use_cases.name: Take Exam
use_cases.description: Student accesses the scheduled exam, answers questions within the time limit, and submits.

use_cases.name: Review Exam Results
use_cases.description: Teacher accesses the dashboard to view auto‑graded scores and analytics for each exam.

use_cases.name: Manage Users and Settings
use_cases.description: Administrator creates, updates, or removes user accounts and configures platform-wide settings.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Teachers can create, edit, and delete question banks.
criteria: All question types can be added, modified, and removed without errors.
Changes are persisted and immediately available for exam scheduling.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Teachers can schedule exams with start/end times and assign them to classes.
criteria: Exam start and end times are enforced by the system.
Only selected students receive notifications and access to the exam.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Students can take timed exams with automatic submission on timeout.
criteria: A visible countdown timer is displayed during the exam.
The exam is auto‑submitted exactly when the timer reaches zero.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: The system automatically grades objective questions and stores results.
criteria: Grades are calculated instantly after submission.
Results are saved and retrievable from the dashboard within 5 seconds.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: The platform must prevent cheating through browser lockdown and monitoring.
criteria: Attempted navigation away from the exam page triggers a warning and logs the event.
Multiple simultaneous logins for the same student are blocked during an exam.

user_stories.story: As a teacher, I want to create and organize question banks, so that I can reuse questions for multiple exams.
acceptance_criteria: Teachers can add, edit, and delete questions within a bank.
Questions are searchable and can be grouped by subject or difficulty.

user_stories.story: As a teacher, I want to schedule exams, so that students know when to take them.
acceptance_criteria: Teachers can set exam date, time, duration, and associate a question bank.
Scheduled exams appear on the student dashboard with countdown timer.

user_stories.story: As a student, I want to take timed tests, so that I can complete assessments within the allocated period.
acceptance_criteria: The test starts only at the scheduled time and enforces the configured duration.
The interface automatically submits answers when time expires.

user_stories.story: As a student, I want to view my results after an exam, so that I can understand my performance.
acceptance_criteria: Results display score, correct/incorrect count, and time taken.
Students can access their result page within 5 minutes of exam completion.

user_stories.story: As an administrator, I want to manage users and exam settings, so that the platform remains organized and secure.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can create, edit, deactivate, and assign roles to user accounts.
Admins can configure global exam parameters such as max attempts and password policies.

user_stories.story: As a system, I want to enforce anti‑cheating measures, so that exam integrity is maintained.
acceptance_criteria: The platform detects multiple simultaneous logins for the same account and blocks them.
During an exam, screen capture, copy‑paste, and navigation away from the test window are disabled.

Database Designer.sql:
CREATE TABLE Users (
    user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT,
    email TEXT,
    role TEXT,
    is_active BOOLEAN
);

CREATE TABLE Exams (
    exam_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    title TEXT,
    scheduled_at DATETIME,
    duration_minutes INTEGER,
    creator_id INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (creator_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Questions (
    question_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    exam_id INTEGER,
    content TEXT,
    max_score REAL,
    question_type TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (exam_id) REFERENCES Exams(exam_id)
);

CREATE TABLE ExamAttempts (
    attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    exam_id INTEGER,
    student_id INTEGER,
    started_at DATETIME,
    completed_at DATETIME,
    score REAL,
    FOREIGN KEY (exam_id) REFERENCES Exams(exam_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

Project Structure.architecture: Microservice‑style monolith: a FastAPI backend serves REST and WebSocket APIs, a React/Vite SPA consumes them, PostgreSQL stores users, exams, questions and results, Redis handles session caching and real‑time exam timers, Celery workers process auto‑grading, Nginx terminates TLS and proxies to backend containers. Docker Compose orchestrates services for development and production.
Project Structure.architecture_diagram:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Client
        UI[React SPA]
    end
    subgraph Server
        API[FastAPI REST & WS]
        Auth[JWT Auth]
        Grader[Celery Workers]
        DB[(PostgreSQL)]
        Cache[Redis]
    end
    subgraph Infra
        Nginx[NGINX]
        Docker[Docker Compose]
    end
    UI -->|HTTPS| Nginx
    Nginx -->|Proxy| API
    API --> Auth
    API -->|CRUD| DB
    API -->|Cache| Cache
    API -->|Async| Grader
    Grader --> DB
    Grader --> Cache
    Nginx --> Docker

Documentation.readme: Online Exam Platform enables teachers to build question banks, schedule timed exams, and auto‑grade. Students log in, take exams within a secure, timed environment, and view results instantly. Admins manage users, roles, and global exam settings. Built with React frontend, Node.js/Express API, PostgreSQL, and JWT authentication.
Documentation.api_documentation: POST /auth/login – body {email, password} returns JWT. GET /exams/:id – fetch exam details (auth required). POST /exams – teacher creates exam schedule. GET /questions/bank – retrieve question bank. POST /answers – submit student answers (auto‑grade). GET /results/:examId – student view results. Admin routes: GET /users, POST /users, PATCH /settings. All endpoints return JSON and use standard HTTP codes.
Documentation.installation: Clone repo, run `npm install` in both /client and /server. Set up PostgreSQL DB, run `npm run migrate`. Create .env with DB_URL, JWT_SECRET, and PORT. Run `npm start` for development (client on 3000, server on 4000).
Documentation.deployment: Containerize with Docker. Build images: `docker build -t exam-client ./client` and `docker build -t exam-server ./server`. Use docker‑compose to launch client, server, and postgres. Configure reverse proxy (NGINX) for HTTPS, set environment variables for production secrets.
Documentation.sprint_plan: Sprint 1 (2w): Auth, user roles, DB schema. Sprint 2 (2w): Question bank CRUD, exam scheduling UI. Sprint 3 (2w): Timed exam engine, auto‑grade logic, cheat‑prevention (browser lockdown, IP monitoring). Sprint 4 (2w): Admin dashboard, reporting, CI/CD pipeline. Sprint 5 (1w): Load testing, bug fixes, documentation.
Documentation.architecture: Frontend: React with Redux, React Router, Material UI. Backend: Node.js/Express REST API, JWT auth, role‑based middleware. Database: PostgreSQL with tables for users, exams, questions, answers, results. Security: HTTPS, CSP, same‑origin, token refresh, exam session token, client‑side lockdown script. Scalability: stateless API, load‑balanced containers, Redis cache for session data.
